sections.h2: Which Indian River County offices touch a tax bill?
sections.html:
The work divides three ways: the Property Appraiser sets values and takes exemption filings, the Tax Collector mails and collects the bills, and a county Value Adjustment Board hears appeals. Recorded deeds sit with the Clerk of the Court.

The Property Appraiser keeps two offices: the Vero office at 1800 27th St., Bldg. B, Vero Beach, (772) 226-1469, and a Sebastian office at 1921 U.S. 1, (772) 226-1133, both staffed Monday through Friday from eight to five. The Tax Collector's tax department answers at (772) 226-1343. The Collector says it acts as an agent for local governments and has no say over assessed value or the amount due.

The Tax Collector's site links to the county's municipalities, which include Vero Beach, Sebastian, Indian River Shores, Orchid and Fellsmere. Houses in any of them are billed by the same county Tax Collector.

sections.h2: How large is the Indian River County tax roll?
sections.html:
The Property Appraiser's home page reports a 2026 certified roll with $51,957,635,233 in just value and $33,819,841,085 in taxable value. It counts 96,241 real parcels and 9,853 tangible personal property accounts.

Exemptions, assessment caps and other reductions explain the gap between those two totals. Your own notice carries the three numbers that govern one parcel: market, assessed and taxable value.

sections.h2: What are the Indian River County due dates and discounts?
sections.html:
Bills go out by November 1, and the early-payment discount falls one step each month until March.

  • November postmark: 4% off
  • December postmark: 3% off
  • January postmark: 2% off
  • February postmark: 1% off
  • March: full gross amount

Silence from the mail is no excuse: the Tax Collector says the owner must see that a bill is received, and asks anyone without one by November 9 to call. Send a written address change to the Property Appraiser, and expect a separate bill for each parcel you own.

Two bill messages deserve attention. A "Do Not Pay" notice means a mortgage company has requested your original bill, and "Back Taxes Remain Unpaid" means delinquent tax also sits on the account. Call (772) 226-1343 to learn the amount.

sections.h2: What if an Indian River County bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The delinquency date is April 1, when a 3% penalty attaches to the gross tax. By May, an advertising fee is added and the account is listed weekly in a local newspaper for three weeks running. Then a certificate has to be sold by June 1.

The Tax Collector sends interested bidders to a county page on a tax certificate sale website. A certificate ranks as a first lien on the parcel. Two years after the April 1 of issue, its holder may seek a deed, and the Clerk then auctions the property under the state's deposit and payment-within-24-hours rules.

The Tax Collector's office adds that no partial payments are taken on current or delinquent real estate bills. An owner who cannot pay in full has three routes: next year's installment plan, a homestead deferral if eligible, or a sale that clears the tax from proceeds.

sections.h2: Does Indian River County offer a four-payment plan?
sections.html:
Yes, when next year's estimated bill exceeds $100. The application is filed ahead of the plan year: the office takes 2026 tax year applications from November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027, and closed the 2025 window on May 1, 2026.

Four bills make up the plan: June (6% discount), September (4.5%), December (3%) and March (no discount). June and September are computed from last year's tax, while December and March absorb the true-up to the new roll. A late first payment may be made in July, minus the 6%. Skip it altogether and the account reverts to a normal November bill.

The office cannot accept an installment outside its month, and a payment that misses its month forfeits the discount. If the house sells mid-plan, the account stays on the plan for that year, so the closing agent needs the list of paid installments. A buyer who prefers an annual bill next year can ask the Tax Collector to drop the account.

sections.h2: What deferral and exemptions are available in Indian River County?
sections.html:
A homestead owner whose age and income qualify can postpone part or all of the bill by applying to the Tax Collector by March 31. Interest accrues on the deferred amount as a lien, and everything becomes payable at death, on a sale of the home, or when homestead status changes.

Homestead filings go to the Property Appraiser by March 1, with permanent Florida residency required on January 1. The appraiser's home page says that applications submitted after September 6 are for the 2027 tax year. The state exemption comes in two tiers, and the school-tax-exempt tier is the first $25,000 only.

On a homestead, the Save Our Homes cap (2.7 percent for 2026) restrains growth. When the home sells, value resets to market the next January 1, so the buyer's bill may look nothing like yours.

sections.h2: Where do I send a petition against an Indian River County value?
sections.html:
File a petition with the Value Adjustment Board by the date printed on your Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, which Florida sets at 25 days after the notices are mailed.

The Property Appraiser's home page links to the county's Value Adjustment Board site. If the appraiser denied an exemption, the state allows a petition 30 days after the denial letter is mailed. Bring comparable sales, photographs and repair estimates with you.

sections.h2: What if the bill arrives after the house has sold?
sections.html:
Bills follow the certified tax roll, so a November notice can land on someone who has already sold. The Tax Collector gives clear directions for that case.

  • A real estate bill for property you no longer own should be forwarded to the new owner or returned to the Tax Collector's office.
  • A business equipment bill is different: if you owned the equipment on January 1, you still owe the tax. If you did not, call the Property Appraiser at (772) 226-1370.
  • Each parcel gets its own bill, so check that the legal description on yours matches everything you own.
  • Address changes go to the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector, and the appraiser offers an online change-of-address form.

Those steps keep a missing or misdirected notice from turning into a delinquent account that a buyer's lender will notice.

sections.h2: What belongs on an Indian River County seller's closing checklist?
sections.html:
Order a payoff and confirm which bill is open. The Tax Collector says the new owner answers for the entire November bill, yet closing agents ordinarily prorate it, giving the buyer a credit for the seller's months. The seller does not send the Tax Collector a partial payment.

  • Look for a back-taxes message on the account.
  • List any installment payments already made.
  • Ask if a deferral lien is attached to the homestead.
  • Check the recorded deeds at the Clerk's office.

The state deed stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and every party on the document can be liable. Where back tax, a deferral lien or a damaged roof complicates a sale, a cash buyer taking the house as-is can have the title company pay the balance.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Indian River County property tax?
faqs.a: Use the county tax payment portal the Tax Collector links from its site. Discounts follow the postmark date, and the tax department at (772) 226-1343 can tell you about other payment options.

faqs.q: When does Indian River County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1, when the 3% penalty is added. In May unpaid accounts are advertised, ahead of a certificate sale due by June 1.

faqs.q: When can I apply for the 2026 tax year installment plan?
faqs.a: Applications for the 2026 tax year run November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027, and the first payment falls in June.

faqs.q: Can I pay part of an Indian River County bill?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Collector says partial payments on current or delinquent real estate bills are not accepted.

faqs.q: Do I owe the whole year's tax if I sell in spring?
faqs.a: The bill goes to the owner, but closing agents normally prorate, so the buyer repays the seller for the months after closing. Check the split on the closing statement.
